statements.t: The Internet financial system is increasingly being built on blockchain infrastructure, and represents a fundamental shift that we believe will result in a profound change to the existing financial system by materially improving efficiency, reducing costs, expanding accessibility, and accelerating innovation.

We believe we are well positioned to benefit from the growth of this emerging, transformative space, and we expect increased adoption and expansion of the Internet financial system to be a key driver of growth in all our products and services, and hence of our overall financial performance.

We expect to continue allocating significant resources to keep our practices aligned with evolving regulations in the U.S. and in the European Union, where our investment firm license from the Spanish regulator has been passported to 15 other EU countries and we have applied for a license under the EU’s DLT Pilot Regime.
We believe increased regulatory certainty will accelerate adoption of tokenized assets; however, regulatory developments may also impose new compliance obligations or increase competition.
Over the medium term, we intend to expand into the traditional finance (“TradFi”) market, which we estimate at over $400 trillion.

We intend to address these barriers by integrating with TradFi platforms and simplifying the user experience, including through custody of tokenized securities by our broker-dealer, and by offering tokenized products, including issuer-led tokenized public equities, that provide more efficient fractional ownership, lower minimum investment thresholds, self-directed management capabilities and additional liquidity…

In connection with becoming a public company, we have hired and expect to continue to hire additional personnel and to implement procedures and processes to address public company regulatory requirements and customary practices.

We have incurred and expect to incur additional annual expenses as a public company for, among other things, hiring of new personnel and fees to outside consultants, and costs related to implementation of an appropriate internal control framework, insurance, and investor relations.

Provision for expected credit losses consists of credit loss expense on our trade receivables, including amounts recognized to adjust our allowance for expected credit losses to management’s current estimate of expected credit losses and receivables written off.

The current-period gain was primarily driven by the 2024 Notes, as the increase in the estimated fair value of the Company’s common stock in anticipation of the Business Combination resulted in holders being expected to convert at the fixed conversion price, which reduced the fair value of the associated derivative to nil.
Share-based compensation expense has been, and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our compensation strategy;
